subject: Transportation Systems
title: Truck Platooning
description: A micro-lesson that makes Truck Platooning usable.

hook.text: Three trucks driving inches apart in a connected convoy. It sounds dangerous. It saves 10% on fuel.

buildup.text: Platooning links trucks electronically. The lead truck brakes; the followers brake simultaneously.

discovery.text: Close spacing reduces aerodynamic drag. The rear trucks draft behind the leader like cyclists in a peloton.

twist.text: Regulation and insurance haven't caught up. Who is liable when a platoon crashes—the lead driver? The software?

climax.text: Several companies tested platooning on highways. Results are promising, but commercial rollout remains slow.

punchline.text: Drafting works for cyclists—and for 40-ton trucks.

quiz.question: How does truck platooning save fuel?
options: Reducing aerodynamic drag by having trucks follow closely together
